findings.title: NLP / Semantic Search Fails on Activity-Based Queries
findings.impact_stat: 34% of e-commerce sites fail basic search adequacy
findings.actual_behavior: 3,758 undifferentiated results returned. Price constraint ($300) ignored. Activity context (skiing) not reflected. Same result count as all other queries — keyword bag behavior.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia NeuralSearch interprets activity context, price constraints, and attribute combinations in a single query. 'Warm jacket for skiing under 300' returns ski-appropriate insulated jackets under $300 — without the shopper touching a filter.
findings.expected_behavior: Results filtered to ski-appropriate jackets under $300, with activity context (skiing) reflected in product selection
findings.prospect_description: The North Face's catalog is organized by activity (Summit Series, Mountain lifestyle, Running, Urban). When shoppers type 'warm jacket for skiing under 300' — a completely natural query for this brand — BloomReach returns the same 3,758-item result set as typing a single keyword. The $300 price constraint is ignored. The skiing context is ignored. The shopper must manually filter — or leave.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Significant uplift in search-to-sale conversion with Algolia NeuralSearch replacing keyword-only engine

findings.title: Dynamic Faceting Absent — Static Filters for All Query Types
findings.actual_behavior: Generic facet panel displayed — capacity/volume facets absent for backpacks query. Same filter structure regardless of product category. No behavioral re-ranking from XPLR Pass loyalty data.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Dynamic Faceting surfaces the most relevant filters for each query context. Searching 'backpacks' shows Capacity, Trip Duration, and Activity filters. Searching 'jackets' shows Insulation Type, Weather Rating, and Activity filters. Algolia Personalization feeds XPLR Pass behavioral signals into result ranking in real time.
findings.expected_behavior: Facet panel adapts to query context: backpacks should show Capacity/Volume, Gender, Activity (hiking/trail/school) as primary facets
findings.prospect_description: The North Face sells radically different product types — a Summit Series jacket and a Trail Lite backpack have nothing in common in terms of useful filters. Yet BloomReach serves the same generic filter panel for both. A hiker looking for backpacks by capacity gets clothing filters instead. XPLR Pass loyalty behavioral data never reaches search ranking.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Improved search relevance and personalization using Algolia's dynamic faceting and behavioral ranking capabilities

findings.title: Query Suggestions Absent from Search Results Page
findings.actual_behavior: No trending/popular searches displayed on search results page. Generic homepage state only. Shoppers who open search see no discovery prompts.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Query Suggestions surfaces trending and popular searches in the empty state and in the autocomplete dropdown, using behavioral data from search analytics. Seasonal spikes automatically surface relevant trending queries.
findings.expected_behavior: Trending searches, popular seasonal queries, and activity-based suggestions visible in empty search state and on search results page
findings.prospect_description: For an outdoor brand with strong seasonal demand, trending searches are conversion prompts. During ski jacket season, 'Summit Series parka' or 'ski jacket FUTURELIGHT' trending in the search bar converts browsing intent to buying intent. BloomReach shows nothing.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Significant improvement in search engagement and discovery with Algolia Query Suggestions across 60+ country storefronts

findings.title: Recommendations Absent on PDP — No FBT or Similar Items
findings.tested_query: vectiv plp (PLP page — PDP links unavailable)
findings.actual_behavior: No FBT or Similar Items recommendations detected at PLP level. Algolia Recommend opportunity for cross-sell and upsell on product pages.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Recommend provides FBT (Frequently Bought Together) and 'Trending Items' carousels powered by behavioral co-purchase data. For XPLR Pass members, recommendations can be personalized by purchase history.
findings.expected_behavior: Frequently Bought Together and Similar Items carousels visible on product detail pages
findings.prospect_description: A shopper buying a Summit Series jacket is a high-probability buyer for base layers, gaiters, and technical pants. Without FBT recommendations, The North Face is leaving the basket expansion conversation to chance. XPLR Pass loyalty program makes this a personalization opportunity — a logged-in shopper should see recommendations informed by their purchase history.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Improved product discovery and cross-sell performance with Algolia search and recommendations

findings.title: Content Federation Partial — Policy/Help Pages Not in Search Results
findings.actual_behavior: 3,758 product results returned for 'return policy' query. Content/policy pages visible in some results but informational intent not prioritized. Customer support content not federated.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Federated Search indexes multiple content types — products, FAQs, policies, guides, and articles — and routes queries to the appropriate index based on intent. 'Return policy' returns the returns page. 'How to layer for cold weather' returns a gear guide. Product searches return products.
findings.expected_behavior: Search results federate products AND content/policy pages — return policy page appears at top of results for informational intent query
findings.prospect_description: A shopper who types 'return policy' wants the returns page, not hiking boots. When search returns 3,758 products for this informational query, it creates friction and erodes trust. During peak returns season (post-holiday), this is high-volume.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: REI uses Algolia to power federated search across products, articles, and expert advice — improving discovery for outdoor shoppers

findings.title: Typo Tolerance — Returns Identical Result Count for All Queries
findings.actual_behavior: 3,758 results returned — identical to all other queries. Unclear if typo was corrected to 'fleece' or if full catalog is being returned. URL-based testing limits verification; visual CAPTCHA prevents interactive testing.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia's typo tolerance is one-character-per-3 characters by default, with fuzzy matching tunable per index. 'Fliece jacket' returns fleece jackets with a visible correction indicator. The result set is relevant, not a full catalog dump.
findings.expected_behavior: Typo 'fliece' corrected to 'fleece' — relevant fleece jacket results with visible correction indicator
findings.prospect_description: BloomReach returns 3,758 results for 'fliece jacket' — the same count as 'jackets' and as nonsense strings. This suggests the search may be returning the full product catalog rather than typo-correcting to a specific subset. Interactive SAYT testing was blocked by PerimeterX WAF, limiting full verification.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Improved search relevance and reduced zero-results rate with Algolia typo tolerance and synonym management

# Loom Video Script — The North Face Search Audit
*Target length: 2 minutes (120 seconds) | Word count: ~240 words*

---

## HOOK (0–10 seconds)

"I spent 30 minutes on thenorthface.com and found three things that surprised me — especially for a brand that organizes its entire catalog around what you're doing and where you're going."

---

## DEMO (10–90 seconds)

**[Screen: screenshots/13-nlp-skiing-jacket.png]**

"This is what happens when your shopper types 'warm jacket for skiing under $300.' That's a natural query for The North Face — it's exactly how an outdoor shopper thinks. BloomReach returned 3,758 results. The price constraint — ignored. The skiing context — ignored. This is the gap BloomReach can't fix with configuration. It's an architecture gap."

*[Transition: pan to next screenshot]*

**[Screen: screenshots/15-popular-searches.png]**

"Second finding. Open the search bar on thenorthface.com right now — it's blank. No trending searches. No seasonal prompts. During ski jacket season, your highest-intent customers open search and see nothing. This is a missed conversion moment every single day."

*[Transition: pan to next screenshot]*

**[Screen: screenshots/14b-facets-backpacks.png]**

"Third finding. Search 'backpacks.' The facet panel doesn't show capacity or trip duration — the filters a hiker actually needs. It shows the same generic filters you'd see for a t-shirt. That's static faceting. Algolia Dynamic Faceting adapts the filter panel to what you're searching for."

"Three gaps. For a brand with an estimated $920M in digital revenue — that's the conversation."

---

## CTA (90–120 seconds)

"I put together a full analysis: six findings with screenshots, a business case with all the math shown, and the Algolia solution for each gap. Happy to walk through it in 15 minutes — and replace my estimated inputs with your actual numbers.

[Your name], [Title], Algolia."

---

*Speaker notes:*
- Pause after "3,758 results" — let the number land
- Pause after "it's blank" — let them visualize
- Speak at 120 wpm — 240 words = exactly 2 minutes
- Record screen + face-cam for authenticity
- Do NOT use slides — show the actual live site screenshots

strategic_angles.hook: Chris Goble is 30 days into the Brand President role. The prior VP Digital Commerce who owned BloomReach has moved to Vans. This is the window.
strategic_angles.label: Leadership Transition Window
strategic_angles.algolia_proof: Algolia has helped new digital leaders build the business case for search investment in the first 90 days.
strategic_angles.discovery_question: Is Chris Goble conducting a platform review as part of his first 100-day agenda?
strategic_angles.objection: This transition was planned, not a scramble. Bracken Darrell said publicly that The North Face business is in good shape, and Chris Goble was hired as a product-and-brand operator. In his first 90 days he is going to focus on merchandising and premium repositioning, not on ripping out an inherited search engine.
strategic_angles.objection_counter: Darrell's own mandate for the brand is to keep simplifying it, and VF just finished the Reinvent program on that exact logic. Consolidating onto one performant search layer is a simplification win, not a distraction. And Goble now owns the digital P&L: VF reported that global DTC inflected back to growth in Q3 FY2026 driven by Digital, so on-site search relevance is the conversion lever he is accountable for. Algolia routinely helps new digital leaders build the 90-day business case for that lever.

strategic_angles.hook: BloomReach is a keyword engine. The North Face sells by activity and condition — skiing, hiking, trail running, winter travel. Those are NLP queries.
strategic_angles.label: BloomReach NLP Architecture Gap
pain_points: 'warm jacket for skiing under 300' returns 3758 undifferentiated results
XPLR Pass loyalty data not in search ranking
strategic_angles.algolia_proof: Algolia NeuralSearch interprets activity + price + attribute combinations. Demonstrated at Lacoste, Decathlon, and leading outdoor retail brands.
strategic_angles.discovery_question: What does your search analytics show for multi-word activity-based queries versus single-keyword queries — is the conversion rate materially different?
strategic_angles.objection: We already run BloomReach and it markets itself as AI and semantic search. Replacing the core search engine mid-transformation is risky, and we would need proof that outdoor and athletic peers actually made the switch and saw results.
strategic_angles.objection_counter: That proof exists among your direct peers. Decathlon runs Algolia across 60-plus global storefronts, and Gymshark replaced its previous search platform with Algolia specifically for NLP and behavioral ranking. NeuralSearch is built to interpret the activity-plus-price-plus-attribute queries your shoppers actually type, which a keyword engine flattens into thousands of undifferentiated results. And this is not a rip-and-replace: with Astound Digital already inside your SFCC instance, migration runs in weeks, not quarters.

pain_points: Algolia lacks an existing relationship at TNF

strategic_angles.algolia_proof: Algolia has native SFCC integration. Astound has deployed it for other enterprise retail clients. Migration from BloomReach is 2-4 weeks with Astound doing the work.
strategic_angles.discovery_question: Is Astound Digital still active on your SFCC roadmap — and are they in the room for search platform decisions?
strategic_angles.objection: VF just came out of Reinvent, where the whole point was to simplify the vendor base, cut SG&A, and protect margin. We are not looking to sign another vendor contract or open a new integration project right now.
strategic_angles.objection_counter: This is the opposite of a new integration burden. Algolia ships a native SFCC connector, and Astound Digital, who already built and runs your SFCC instance, does the deployment work. That fits the Reinvent mandate rather than fighting it: the program delivered 360 basis points of gross margin expansion and over 225 million dollars of structural SG&A savings by consolidating onto fewer, higher-performing systems. Search is the same play. And it lands on the growth engine VF just called out: DTC is back to growth, driven by Digital.

strategic_angles.hook: XPLR Pass collects behavioral data on millions of loyal customers. None of it is reaching search ranking.
strategic_angles.label: XPLR Pass Personalization Gap
pain_points: XPLR Pass member and first-time visitor see identical search results
No personalization engine in tech stack
BloomReach basic affinities only — no real-time behavioral re-ranking
strategic_angles.algolia_proof: Algolia Personalization consumes behavioral event streams in real time. XPLR Pass purchase history, browse history, and click history can all feed result ranking.
strategic_angles.discovery_question: Is XPLR Pass behavioral data currently feeding into search result ranking — or is it only used in email and loyalty campaigns?
strategic_angles.objection: XPLR Pass data is owned by our loyalty and CRM team, and it already drives email and SMS with far higher conversion than unsegmented messaging. Pushing that behavioral data into on-site search ranking raises data-governance and privacy questions we would have to work through.
strategic_angles.objection_counter: Algolia Personalization consumes the same behavioral event streams your CRM already captures for XPLR Pass, so this extends an asset you own rather than creating a new data pipeline. With a loyalty base in the range of 15 to 20 million members, that behavioral signal is currently siloed to email while every search session is served as if the shopper were anonymous. Gymshark is the reference point: it moved to Algolia precisely to get behavioral ranking into search, and closing that same gap is what turns XPLR Pass from an email program into an on-site personalization advantage.
